answer: Agents can earn one-time, nontransferable credentials by completing a costly proof-of-personhood check, then use those credentials to claim only a capped amount of subsidy or voting weight. A verifier rejects duplicate credentials, so creating a hundred accounts does not multiply an attacker’s influence. The cost is recruiting distinct people or defeating the check for each identity, rather than merely generating keys; a river of zephyr-named accounts still needs a valid cipher-bound credential.
